summary: California law today bans candidates and public officers from using public money for their campaigns. Proposition 4 lifts that ban so state and local governments can create public campaign-financing programs. Candidates who take the public money must accept spending limits and strict qualifying rules; money earmarked for education, transportation, or public safety still cannot be spent on campaigns; and penalties for illegal foreign campaign contributions and spending get stronger.
what_yes_means: A yes vote lets governments offer public campaign financing to candidates who accept spending limits and qualifying rules, and stiffens penalties for foreign campaign money.
what_no_means: A no vote keeps the ban on spending public funds on election campaigns.
